items.title: AI Latent Reasoning:  Sep-Latent Token Compression
items.summary: By applying a progressive Attention-Decay mask that selectively starves intermediate reasoning tokens of attention during training, Sep-Latent forces the transformer to compress multi-step logical states into structural separator anchors, and aligns these compressed states with an MLP-projected continuous latent stream via all-layer Euclidean self-distillation. Paired with a dynamic LM-head exit gate that autonomously terminates silent computation based on query complexity, Sep-Latent keeps latent vectors grounded on the vocabulary manifold, cuts training GPU memory by over 50%, and achieves 56.8% accuracy on GSM8k-Aug using an average of just 5.4 tokens; outperforming both explicit CoT (at nearly 5× token compression) and state-of-the-art implicit baselines in accuracy, speed, and symbolic robustness. All rights w/ authors: Sep-Latent: Separator Tokens as Natural Compression Anchors for Implicit Reasoning Yinlong Xu1,2, Jianfeng Huang2, Zhengdong Zhou2, Mingjie Lin2 Fuyu Lv2, Dan Ou2, Hongxia Xu1*, Jian Wu1* from 1 College of Computer Science and Technology, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China 2 Alibaba Group, Hangzhou, China arXiv:2610.22924 #aiexplained #discoverai #airesearch

items.title: What Survives When AI Can Build Anything? (with Dr. Richard Socher)
items.summary: #aiforscience #superintelligence #agenticai In Episode #1037, Dr. Richard Socher (CEO and Co-Founder of Recursive) joins @JonKrohnLearns to make the case for automating the scientific method itself. Richard’s startup came out of stealth this year with over half a billion dollars raised to build recursively self-improving superintelligence, and his new book, The Eureka Machine, is already a national bestseller. He also co-founded You.com and the venture firm AIX Ventures, was chief scientist at Salesforce, taught the first university course anywhere on neural networks for NLP, and helped build the ImageNet dataset. In this episode, he traces how AI keeps replacing hand-crafted expertise with scale, lays out the four pillars of his Eureka Machine, argues that hallucinations can be a feature for science, explains why recursive self-improvement within a year or two still rules out an overnight takeoff, and names the software and jobs he expects to endure. This episode is brought to you by: • Palo Alto Networks: http://paloaltonetworks.com/idira • Dell Technologies: http://Dell.com/desksideagenticai • Anthropic: https://claude.ai/superdata • Origin: https://www.originhq.com/sds Interested in sponsoring a SuperDataScience Podcast episode? Email natalie@superdatascience.com for sponsorship information. In this episode you will learn: • (00:00:00) Introduction • (00:02:40) What Recursive is automating, and the two forms of RSI • (00:20:56) The four pillars of the Eureka Machine • (00:30:56) Turning sciences into engineering disciplines • (00:41:04) Why RSI does not mean an overnight takeoff • (00:57:46) Constructive optimism, and the future as a construction game Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1037

items.title: Extract data from MRI reports privately with Sparrow
items.summary: Many organizations won't send medical reports to a public cloud API, yet the results still get retyped by hand. In this video, Sparrow turns an MRI lumbar spine report into structured data: disc levels with grades, measurements as numbers, and the full impression. Sparrow is open source and runs on infrastructure you control, on your own machines or a private cloud GPU, so patient data stays inside your environment. This video uses the online version with a synthetic report. Try it online: https://sparrow.katanaml.io Sparrow on GitHub: https://github.com/katanaml/sparrow Want this on your documents? We set it up on your infrastructure and run a pilot: https://katanaml.io/consulting.html More industry videos: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMhQwmybML_A Chapters: 0:00 The problem and why it stays private 2:30 Running the extraction 2:45 The result Sample document: synthetic MRI report created for this video. All names and values are fictional. #Sparrow #OpenSource #MedicalReports
